target_customer: Employers hiring entry-level customer support and operations staff, who pay per month for a screening assessment
problem: Hiring entry-level support and ops staff means reading thousands of applications, and resumes poorly predict job performance.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for pre-employment assessments (launch offer of a discounted first month)
product_category: Pre-employment work sample assessments for support roles

founders.name: Dean Yim
previous_startups: Earlier company where the founders read about 25,000 applications for entry-level ops and sales roles (name not given)
founders.background_notes: YC launch post author. Secondary search summaries mention an early Robinhood role but no opened source confirms it, so prior employers are left empty.

founders.name: Paul Gut
previous_startups: Same earlier company as Dean Yim
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web based interactive work simulation with automatic scoring and benchmarking against top employees; standard product engineering plus assessment design.

defensibility.rationale: Benchmark data from customers' top performers could compound, but assessments were copyable by established pre-hire vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in sources. The YC page lists it as acquired, but no buyer or date was found.

market_need_then: The founders reported their own interview to hire rate rising from 18 percent to 48 percent after building the tool for their own hiring (YC launch post); no external demand data found.

branding.domain_note: Used loopsupport.com; the site returned a 503 when fetched.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name that collides with Loop Returns, Loop Email and many others in search; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Loop Support built a 30 minute work sample to screen entry-level support and ops applicants, launched through YC in 2017 and stayed a team of about seven. The YC directory lists it as acquired, but no buyer, date or price could be found, and aggregators show only a tiny seed and a company that still lists itself as alive. Secondary profiles suggest it later offered staffed support teams, so its story is unclear and no failure or success factor is supported.
notes: CB Insights lists a seed of about $120K dated 2017-08 (two rounds, $120K total) with Y Combinator, Palm Drive Capital and El Cap; the round rests on this single database. Crunchbase names Nimble Ventures instead; Seedtable says 1.0 million and Wellfound 3 million, so figures conflict and a gap may exist. Status conflict: YC says Acquired; CB Insights says alive. No acquirer found. Search summary profiles say it later sold outsourced customer support teams; unverified and not recorded as a pivot. No competitor coverage dated to 2017 found; undated alternative lists named Talentpair, Namely and Covey. Own site returned 503.
